title: Situational choice
description: A choice the player or GM makes when a roll happens (advantage, cover, a GM's bonus, pushing yourself) or when a change arrives (a reaction that halves one attack's damage), declared in game data so apps can offer it without knowing the game. Formulas see the selected value as `situational.<id>`.

rolls.description: Roll tags this choice is offered for. A tag matches itself and every tag below it.

incoming.description: Incoming changes this choice is offered for, matched as an incoming-change effect's target is: an `adjust` whose field is one of `fields` (if given) and with a tag matching one of `tags` (if given). The receiving player selects it on the change (`situational` on an `adjust`); its incoming-change effects then apply while that change is routed.

scope.description: Incoming changes only: how far a selection reaches. `change` (default): the change it is selected on. `batch`: selected on one change of a batch, its incoming-change effects reach that change and every later adjust of the batch its `incoming` matches (an attack's damage types), and each `add` among them is worked out once and spent over those changes, never past 0: what one change doesn't take carries to the next.

available.description: When the choice is offered: a condition on the character (fields and `character`), checked before any roll. Absent means always.

effects.description: Effects that apply while this choice is selected (boolean) or non-default (integer, enum): its roll effects on a roll it is selected for, its incoming-change effects on a change it is selected for. The selected value is visible as `situational.<id>`.

changes.description: Incoming changes only: what choosing it costs or gains (spend a resource, mark a once-a-scene use, damage a held shield, offer a follow-up). Applied to the receiving character once per batch that selects it, however many changes do, after the batch's last change. Formulas see the character as the batch left it, `situational` and `batch`; a `setState` or `adjustState` also sees `item` and `self` per matched copy.

situationalChange.description: A change a situational choice makes: `set` (`field`, `value`) or `adjust` (`field`, `by`, optional `tags`) of the character's input fields, `setState` (`key`, `value`) or `adjustState` (`key`, `by`) of held copies named by `copies` (and optionally `limit`), or `offerFollowUp` of a rules follow-up (`followUp`, optional `params`). `when` skips it unless it holds. Its adjust is routed without incoming-change effects.

copies.description: setState, adjustState: the copies whose state changes, as a change's `copies` query: the copies of `type` (local or qualified; inventory, then features, each in file order) whose `where` holds with `item` and `self` bound, at the batch's end. `where`, `value` and `by` are evaluated per match, in the choice's pack, with `item`, `self`, `situational` and `batch`. No match is not an error.

limit.description: With `copies`: change at most this many matches.

key.description: setState, adjustState: a state key the content type declares (numeric for adjustState).

followUp.description: A rules follow-up's ID, local or `<pack>:<id>`.

params.description: Formulas for the follow-up's action parameters, replacing the declaration's own.
